screen1-a1.where: Top row, far left: a small Spanish flag with the number 1 next to it.
screen1-a1.expectation: I think it opens something about my Spanish course, maybe a list to switch course. I do not know what the 1 is counting.
screen1-a1.cue: The flag means Spanish. Nothing tells me what the 1 means or that pressing it opens anything.

first_pass.why: A flag and a bare number. The flag I can name; the number has no unit and no label, so I cannot tell if this is a course switcher, a level, or a score.
first_pass.solution: Put a word next to the number, for example 'Spanish - Score 1', and make it look like something that opens a list (a small down arrow).

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows what it is for and what the number means
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the flag at the top-left once. Look at what opens. Then press the phone's Back button.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make plain what the flag was for, or still leaves the number unexplained
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly shows what the flag is for and what the number counts
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the flag at the top-left. A panel dropped down showing my Spanish course (outlined), '+ Course', a progress bar from 1 to 2 with 'Your Spanish Score is 1', 'MORE ABOUT SCORE', and 'New Courses': Math, Music, Chess.

screen1-a1.closing_comment: The panel says literally that the 1 is my Spanish Score and that the flag is for my courses. After one press it is clear and I would remember it.

screen1-a2.where: Top row, second from left: a grey flame with the number 1.
screen1-a2.expectation: Probably opens a page about a streak count. I am inferring 'streak' from the convention of flames in games, not from anything written.
screen1-a2.cue: A flame picture and a number. No word.

first_pass.why: A flame does not literally mean 'days in a row'. It is a metaphor (keeping a fire going). The number has no unit. It is also grey, which could mean disabled or could mean 'not done today' - I cannot tell which.
first_pass.solution: Write '1 day streak' or at least 'days' next to the number. Explain what grey means.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the flame tells you what it counts
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the flame in the top row. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens still does not tell you what the flame and its number mean
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens says plainly what the flame and number are
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the grey flame, which showed 0 on my phone. A 'Streak' page opened: '0 day streak!', a card 'You're out of Streak Freezes! GET MORE', and a Streak Calendar with some days marked with blue ice drops. The X closed it.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: The page says plainly that the flame is a day streak and the number is days. The flame on the main screen still has no word, and the blue ice drops on the calendar are a new unexplained picture.

screen1-a3.where: Top row, third: a blue gem with 520.
screen1-a3.expectation: Opens something about my gems, probably the shop where they are spent.
screen1-a3.cue: A gem picture and a number. No word.

first_pass.why: I can name the object (a gem) but a gem is standing in for an in-app currency. The picture does not say it is money or that pressing it opens a shop.
first_pass.solution: Label it 'Gems: 520' and make the tap target say what it opens, e.g. 'Shop'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the stone tells you what it is and what it is for
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the blue stone in the top row. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not say what the stones are or what pressing the stone was for
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens makes plain what the stones are and why you would press it
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the blue stone. The 'Shop' page opened with 644 next to the same blue stone at the top-right. On it, 'Free Chest - Watch an ad to earn up to 15 gems' tells me the stones are gems. The X closed it.

screen1-a3.closing_comment: It opened the shop, which was my guess, and the shop calls them gems. The stone on the main screen still has no word next to it.

screen1-a4.where: Top row, far right: a pink battery-like shape with a lightning bolt and 25.
screen1-a4.expectation: Opens something about energy or battery. I do not know what this energy is used for in the app.
screen1-a4.cue: A lightning/battery picture and 25. No word.

first_pass.why: It looks like my phone battery indicator, which is confusing because the real battery is in the status bar right above it. I would not know this is an in-app resource that runs out when I do lessons.
first_pass.solution: Write 'Energy 25' and give a one-line explanation of what energy is for.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows it is an app thing (not the phone battery) and what the number is
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the pink bolt-and-battery at the top-right. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens still leaves you unsure what it is or what the number means
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens makes plain what it is and what the number means
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the pink bolt at the top-right. A page titled 'Energy' opened with a bar reading '25 / 25' and ways to get more energy. The X closed it.

screen1-a4.closing_comment: Now I know it is the app's 'Energy' and that 25 is out of a maximum of 25, so it is not my phone battery. The page still does not say what energy is used for.

screen1-a5.where: Large green banner under the top row: 'SECTION 1, UNIT 1  Order at a café'.
screen1-a5.expectation: It opens details about the current unit or a list of sections. The text tells me where I am but not what pressing it does.
screen1-a5.cue: The words 'SECTION 1, UNIT 1' and 'Order at a café'.

first_pass.why: The text is literal and clear as a title. But it looks like a heading, not a button. I would not know it is pressable, or whether it opens the unit, the course map, or starts a lesson.
first_pass.solution: Add a visible action word or arrow, for example 'See all sections >'.

test_cases.targets: whether you can tell it can be pressed, and whether pressing it does what you expected
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the words on the green bar at the top (not the small notebook at its right end). See what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: nothing on the bar told you it could be pressed, or what opened was not what you expected from the words
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opened is what you expected from the words on the bar
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the words 'Order at a café' on the green bar. The bar pressed down a little, and after a few seconds a page titled 'Spanish Course' opened, showing Section 1, Section 2 and Section 3 cards. The X at the top-left closed it and took me back to the path.

screen1-a5.closing_comment: What opened was one of my guesses, a list of sections, so it did what I thought. But nothing on the bar says it opens anything. It still looks like a title, so I only found out by pressing it.

screen1-a6.where: Right end of the green banner: a white icon of a notebook/page with lines.
screen1-a6.expectation: Maybe opens notes or a guide for this unit. It could also be a list view.
screen1-a6.cue: A picture of a lined page. No word.

first_pass.why: A lined page could mean notes, a guide, a list, or a document. I cannot tell which from the picture alone.
first_pass.solution: Put the word 'Guide' (or whatever it really is) under or beside the icon.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the notebook settles which of your guesses it is
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the small notebook at the right end of the green bar. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you guessed, or still does not tell you what the notebook stands for
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches one of your guesses and you would remember it next time
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the small notebook at the right end of the green bar. A page opened with 'SECTION 1, UNIT 1  Order at a café' and 'KEY PHRASES': Spanish sentences with English translations and speaker icons. The X closed it.

screen1-a6.closing_comment: It was one of my guesses, a guide or notes for the unit, and I would remember it now. The picture still does not say 'Key phrases', so a first-time user has to press it to find out.

screen1-a7.where: Left edge under the banner: a green cartoon character partly hidden behind a black-and-yellow skull badge with a red exclamation mark.
screen1-a7.expectation: No idea. It could be a profile, an alert, an event, or an advert.
screen1-a7.cue: Nothing I can read. A cartoon, a skull logo, and a red '!'.

first_pass.why: Three pictures stacked on each other, none of which names a thing I recognise in this app, plus a red '!' that says 'something is urgent' without saying what. I would not press it because I cannot predict what it starts.
first_pass.solution: Replace it with text saying what it is, e.g. 'Brawl Stars event - 13 days left', and remove the unexplained exclamation mark or say what it is warning about.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the badge tells you what it is and what the red mark was about
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the cartoon owl-and-skull picture at the left, under the green bar. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left, or the lower blue text button if there is no X. Do NOT press any button that says it claims on or opens another game.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens still does not make plain what this is, or it takes you somewhere you could not have predicted
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens makes plain what it is and you could predict it next time
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the owl-and-skull picture. On my phone the red exclamation mark was not there, and the pill under it said 'Ended'. A page titled 'Brawl Stars Quest', marked 'INCOMPLETE', opened: a seven-day list of rewards (Day 1 'Brawl Stars Chaos Drops' with a tick and an open-outside icon, Day 2 '15 gems', Day 3 'Epic Chest', and so on). The X closed it.

screen1-a7.closing_comment: Now I know it is a seven-day reward event linked to another game called Brawl Stars. I could not have predicted that from the picture, but I would recognise it next time. The red mark was not on my phone, so I could not learn what it was about.

screen1-a8.where: Top of the winding path: a round green button with a white star inside a green ring (as it looks on the running app).
screen1-a8.expectation: Starts or continues the current lesson, because it is the only coloured one at the start of the path.
screen1-a8.cue: It is green while the rest are grey, and it is first on the path. There are no words.

first_pass.why: A star does not mean 'lesson'. Stars usually mean favourite or rating. I work it out only from the colour difference and position, not from the picture.
first_pass.solution: Put 'Start' or 'Lesson 2' on or under the current button.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the green star shows plainly that it is a lesson
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the round green star button near the top of the path. Read what appears. Do NOT press the button inside what appears; press on an empty part of the path to close it.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not say it is a lesson, or you still could not have known from the star
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears says plainly it is your next lesson
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the green star button. After a moment a green box appeared under it: 'Order at a café', 'Lesson 2 of 3', and a button 'CONTINUE +20 XP'. I did not press the button. I pressed an empty part of the path and the box closed.

screen1-a8.closing_comment: Once pressed, it says plainly that it is lesson 2 of 3. The star itself still does not say 'lesson'. I learn that only after I press it.

screen1-a9.where: Purple pill under the cartoon on the left: '13 days'.
screen1-a9.expectation: Probably shows how long the thing above it (the skull event) lasts. Pressing it maybe opens the same thing.

first_pass.why: '13 days' is literal but has no subject: 13 days of what? Left? Done? It is attached to the thing I already could not identify.
first_pass.solution: Say '13 days left in event' and name the event.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the pill tells you what the time count refers to
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the purple pill under the owl-and-skull picture. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not tell you what the days referred to
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens says plainly what the days count
test_cases.what_happened: My pill said 'Ended', not a number of days. I pressed it and the same 'Brawl Stars Quest' page opened, and that page said 'INCOMPLETE'. Nothing on it gives a day count or an end date. The X closed it.

screen1-a9.closing_comment: The pill says 'Ended' and the page it opens says 'INCOMPLETE', and neither says what ended or what the days in the pill were counting. The two words contradict each other.

screen1-a11.where: On the path, the second button: a round grey button with a grey star (as on the running app).
screen1-a11.expectation: A locked lesson. Pressing it probably tells me it is locked.
screen1-a11.cue: Grey colour compared with the green one. No text, no lock picture.

first_pass.why: Grey suggests unavailable but nothing says so. The star again does not say 'lesson'.
first_pass.solution: Show a lock symbol and a label such as 'Lesson 3 - locked'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing a grey star says it is a lesson and that it is locked
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the first round grey star button below the green one. Read what appears. Press an empty part of the path to close it.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not say what the grey star is, or does not say it is locked
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears says plainly it is a lesson that is locked
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the first grey star below the green one. A grey box grew out of it and said 'Order at a café', 'Complete all levels above to unlock this!', with a grey 'LOCKED' button. Pressing empty path closed it after a second press settled. The box covered the next grey star and the chest while it was open.

screen1-a11.closing_comment: It says plainly that it is locked and why. It says 'levels', while the green one said 'Lesson 2 of 3', so the app uses two words for what looks like the same kind of button.

screen1-a15.expectation: No idea. It is not the green owl used everywhere else. Maybe a different product or an AI feature.
screen1-a15.cue: Nothing. A picture of a bird and no word.

screen1-a19.closing_comment: It was the 'something social' reading, so one of my guesses. I could not have told in advance whether it was messages, likes or a feed. Now I know it is a feed.

screen1-a20.closing_comment: It was a short 'more' list, as I expected. The red dot is still unexplained: now both items have one and neither says what is new. Back did not close the sheet, which I did not expect.

screen6-a6.closing_comment: It was one of my guesses, a guide or notes for the unit, and I would remember it now. The picture still does not say 'Key phrases', so a first-time user has to press it to find out.

screen6-a7.where: Left edge under the banner: a green cartoon character partly hidden behind a black-and-yellow skull badge with a red exclamation mark.
screen6-a7.expectation: No idea. It could be a profile, an alert, an event, or an advert.
screen6-a7.cue: Nothing I can read. A cartoon, a skull logo, and a red '!'.

first_pass.why: Three pictures stacked on each other, none of which names a thing I recognise in this app, plus a red '!' that says 'something is urgent' without saying what. I would not press it because I cannot predict what it starts.
first_pass.solution: Replace it with text saying what it is, e.g. 'Brawl Stars event - 13 days left', and remove the unexplained exclamation mark or say what it is warning about.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the badge tells you what it is and what the red mark was about
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the cartoon owl-and-skull picture at the left, under the green bar. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left, or the lower blue text button if there is no X. Do NOT press any button that says it claims on or opens another game.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens still does not make plain what this is, or it takes you somewhere you could not have predicted
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens makes plain what it is and you could predict it next time
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the owl-and-skull picture. On my phone the red exclamation mark was not there, and the pill under it said 'Ended'. A page titled 'Brawl Stars Quest', marked 'INCOMPLETE', opened: a seven-day list of rewards (Day 1 'Brawl Stars Chaos Drops' with a tick and an open-outside icon, Day 2 '15 gems', Day 3 'Epic Chest', and so on). The X closed it.

screen6-a7.closing_comment: Now I know it is a seven-day reward event linked to another game called Brawl Stars. I could not have predicted that from the picture, but I would recognise it next time. The red mark was not on my phone, so I could not learn what it was about.

screen6-a8.where: Top of the winding path: a round green button with a white star inside a green ring (as it looks on the running app).
screen6-a8.expectation: Starts or continues the current lesson, because it is the only coloured one at the start of the path.
screen6-a8.cue: It is green while the rest are grey, and it is first on the path. There are no words.

first_pass.why: A star does not mean 'lesson'. Stars usually mean favourite or rating. I work it out only from the colour difference and position, not from the picture.
first_pass.solution: Put 'Start' or 'Lesson 2' on or under the current button.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the green star shows plainly that it is a lesson
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the round green star button near the top of the path. Read what appears. Do NOT press the button inside what appears; press on an empty part of the path to close it.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not say it is a lesson, or you still could not have known from the star
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears says plainly it is your next lesson
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the green star button. After a moment a green box appeared under it: 'Order at a café', 'Lesson 2 of 3', and a button 'CONTINUE +20 XP'. I did not press the button. I pressed an empty part of the path and the box closed.

screen6-a8.closing_comment: Once pressed, it says plainly that it is lesson 2 of 3. The star itself still does not say 'lesson'. I learn that only after I press it.

screen6-a9.where: Purple pill under the cartoon on the left: '13 days'.
screen6-a9.expectation: Probably shows how long the thing above it (the skull event) lasts. Pressing it maybe opens the same thing.

first_pass.why: '13 days' is literal but has no subject: 13 days of what? Left? Done? It is attached to the thing I already could not identify.
first_pass.solution: Say '13 days left in event' and name the event.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the pill tells you what the time count refers to
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the purple pill under the owl-and-skull picture. Read what opens. Close it with the X at the top-left.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not tell you what the days referred to
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens says plainly what the days count
test_cases.what_happened: My pill said 'Ended', not a number of days. I pressed it and the same 'Brawl Stars Quest' page opened, and that page said 'INCOMPLETE'. Nothing on it gives a day count or an end date. The X closed it.

screen6-a9.closing_comment: The pill says 'Ended' and the page it opens says 'INCOMPLETE', and neither says what ended or what the days in the pill were counting. The two words contradict each other.

screen6-a12.where: Inside the green popup 'Order at a café  Lesson 2 of 3': white button 'CONTINUE +20 XP'.
screen6-a12.expectation: Continues with lesson 2 of 3 and I earn 20 XP for it.

first_pass.why: Literal. This popup finally tells me what the green star button is: a lesson.

screen6-a13.where: On the path, left side: a grey treasure chest.
screen6-a13.expectation: A reward chest you open after finishing lessons. It is grey, so probably not available yet.
screen6-a13.cue: The chest picture and grey colour.

first_pass.why: I can name the object - a chest - but a chest standing for 'a reward' is an idea, not a function. Nothing says when it opens or what is inside.
first_pass.solution: Add text like 'Reward - unlocks after 10 lessons'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the chest tells you what it gives and when you can open it
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the grey treasure chest on the path. Read what appears. Press an empty part of the path to close it.

test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the grey chest on the path. A grey box appeared under it saying 'Complete 10 more lessons to unlock this chest!'. Pressing an empty part of the path closed it.

screen6-a13.closing_comment: It now tells me plainly when the chest opens. It still does not say what is inside, so part of my question is not answered.

screen6-a14.where: On the path, the second button: a round grey button with a grey star (as on the running app).
screen6-a14.expectation: A locked lesson. Pressing it probably tells me it is locked.
screen6-a14.cue: Grey colour compared with the green one. No text, no lock picture.

first_pass.why: Grey suggests unavailable but nothing says so. The star again does not say 'lesson'.
first_pass.solution: Show a lock symbol and a label such as 'Lesson 3 - locked'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing a grey star says it is a lesson and that it is locked
test_cases.action: On the main screen, press the first round grey star button below the green one. Read what appears. Press an empty part of the path to close it.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears does not say what the grey star is, or does not say it is locked
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears says plainly it is a lesson that is locked
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the first grey star below the green one. A grey box grew out of it and said 'Order at a café', 'Complete all levels above to unlock this!', with a grey 'LOCKED' button. Pressing empty path closed it after a second press settled. The box covered the next grey star and the chest while it was open.

screen6-a14.closing_comment: It says plainly that it is locked and why. It says 'levels', while the green one said 'Lesson 2 of 3', so the app uses two words for what looks like the same kind of button.

screen6-a15.cue: Nothing. A picture of a bird and no word.

first_pass.why: It does not depict a thing I can name as a function. It is a different bird from the app's owl, so I cannot even guess it by association. It is also out of the tag order (a15 sits between a19 and a20), but that is only the tags.
first_pass.solution: Put a text label under every bottom-bar icon, including this one.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected and you would recognise the bird next time
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the bird in the bottom row. A page titled 'Subscription' opened, comparing plans: 'Super', 'Super Family' and 'Lite (with ads)', each with a 'TRY FOR $0.00' button. I pressed nothing on it and went back with the house.

screen6-a15.closing_comment: A bird for paid subscription plans is not something I could have guessed. Knowing it now does not make the picture say 'Subscription'. I would still need a text label.

screen6-a16.expectation: Home - the screen I am on now.
screen6-a16.cue: A house means home, and it is highlighted.

first_pass.why: House for home is literal enough and the highlight matches the screen I am on.

screen6-a17.closing_comment: The chest is connected to rewards, which was my reading, but the page is 'Quests', and I would not have guessed that from a chest. The chest on the path means something else again.

screen6-a18.where: Bottom bar, third: a brown trophy cup.
screen6-a18.expectation: Rankings or a leaderboard, because a trophy means competing.

first_pass.why: A trophy is a real object and it points in the right direction, but it could also mean achievements or awards. Without a word I am choosing between those.

screen6-a18.closing_comment: It was the leaderboard, which was my first reading, and I would recognise the trophy next time.

screen6-a19.where: Bottom bar, fourth: a pink speech bubble with a heart inside.
screen6-a19.expectation: Something social - messages, likes, or friends. I am not sure which.

test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the heart-in-a-bubble. A page titled 'Feed' opened, with friend slots, 'Start Friend Streaks', 'Celebrate achievements with friends! ADD FRIENDS', and news-style cards ('CULTURE 8 hours'). The house took me back.

screen6-a19.closing_comment: It was the 'something social' reading, so one of my guesses. I could not have told in advance whether it was messages, likes or a feed. Now I know it is a feed.

screen6-a20.expectation: A 'more' menu with other options, and the red dot means something new is in there.
screen6-a20.cue: Three dots usually mean 'more'. The red dot usually means a notification.

first_pass.why: Three dots is a common convention so I get the general idea, but 'more' is not a destination. The red dot tells me something is new without saying what.
first_pass.solution: Label it 'More' and say what the notification is about.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows what is behind it and what the red dot was about
test_cases.action: Press the purple three-dot circle at the right of the bottom row. Read what appears. Press the phone's Back button to close it, then the house.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears is a short list you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the purple three-dot circle. A short sheet slid up from the bottom with two items: 'Profile' and 'Video Call'. Each had its own small red dot. The phone's Back button did not close the sheet (two screenshots after it, still open). Pressing the house closed it.

screen6-a20.closing_comment: It was a short 'more' list, as I expected. The red dot is still unexplained: now both items have one and neither says what is new. Back did not close the sheet, which I did not expect.

screen7-a1.expectation: I think it opens something about my Spanish course, maybe a list to switch course. I do not know what the 1 is counting.
screen7-a1.cue: The flag means Spanish. Nothing tells me what the 1 means or that pressing it opens anything.

first_pass.why: A flag and a bare number. The flag I can name; the number has no unit and no label, so I cannot tell if this is a course switcher, a level, or a score.
first_pass.solution: Put a word next to the number, for example 'Spanish - Score 1', and make it look like something that opens a list (a small down arrow).

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows what it is for and what the number means

test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens does not make plain what the flag was for, or still leaves the number unexplained
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens plainly shows what the flag is for and what the number counts
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the flag at the top-left. A panel dropped down showing my Spanish course (outlined), '+ Course', a progress bar from 1 to 2 with 'Your Spanish Score is 1', 'MORE ABOUT SCORE', and 'New Courses': Math, Music, Chess.

screen7-a1.closing_comment: The panel says literally that the 1 is my Spanish Score and that the flag is for my courses. After one press it is clear and I would remember it.

screen7-a2.where: Top row, second from left: a grey flame with the number 1.

first_pass.solution: Write '1 day streak' or at least 'days' next to the number. Explain what grey means.

test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens says plainly what the flame and number are

screen7-a2.closing_comment: The page says plainly that the flame is a day streak and the number is days. The flame on the main screen still has no word, and the blue ice drops on the calendar are a new unexplained picture.

screen7-a3.where: Top row, third: a blue gem with 520.

screen7-a3.closing_comment: It opened the shop, which was my guess, and the shop calls them gems. The stone on the main screen still has no word next to it.

first_pass.why: A trophy is a real object and it points in the right direction, but it could also mean achievements or awards. Without a word I am choosing between those.
first_pass.solution: Label it 'Leaderboard'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it settles which of your readings is right
test_cases.action: Press the cup/trophy shape in the bottom row. Read what opens. Then press the house.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is not what you expected, or you still could not tell which it would be next time
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens matches what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the trophy. A page opened with a three-person ranking and 'Finish 2 lessons to start competing on Leaderboards!'. The house took me back.

screen35-a18.closing_comment: It was the leaderboard, which was my first reading, and I would recognise the trophy next time.

screen35-a19.where: Bottom bar, fourth: a pink speech bubble with a heart inside.
screen35-a19.expectation: Something social - messages, likes, or friends. I am not sure which.
screen35-a19.cue: A heart and a speech bubble.

first_pass.why: Two symbols combined. A heart could be likes, lives, health or favourites; a speech bubble is chat. I cannot tell what the page will be.
first_pass.solution: Label it with a word ('Feed', 'Friends', etc.).

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it settles which of your readings is right
test_cases.action: Press the heart-in-a-bubble in the bottom row. Read what opens. Then press the house.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what opens is none of the things you guessed, or you could not tell which in advance
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what opens is what you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the heart-in-a-bubble. A page titled 'Feed' opened, with friend slots, 'Start Friend Streaks', 'Celebrate achievements with friends! ADD FRIENDS', and news-style cards ('CULTURE 8 hours'). The house took me back.

screen35-a19.closing_comment: It was the 'something social' reading, so one of my guesses. I could not have told in advance whether it was messages, likes or a feed. Now I know it is a feed.

screen35-a20.where: Bottom bar, far right: a purple circle with three dots and a small red dot on its corner.
screen35-a20.expectation: A 'more' menu with other options, and the red dot means something new is in there.
screen35-a20.cue: Three dots usually mean 'more'. The red dot usually means a notification.

first_pass.why: Three dots is a common convention so I get the general idea, but 'more' is not a destination. The red dot tells me something is new without saying what.
first_pass.solution: Label it 'More' and say what the notification is about.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing it shows what is behind it and what the red dot was about
test_cases.action: Press the purple three-dot circle at the right of the bottom row. Read what appears. Press the phone's Back button to close it, then the house.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: what appears is not what you expected, or the red dot is still unexplained
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what appears is a short list you expected
test_cases.what_happened: I pressed the purple three-dot circle. A short sheet slid up from the bottom with two items: 'Profile' and 'Video Call'. Each had its own small red dot. The phone's Back button did not close the sheet (two screenshots after it, still open). Pressing the house closed it.

screen35-a20.closing_comment: It was a short 'more' list, as I expected. The red dot is still unexplained: now both items have one and neither says what is new. Back did not close the sheet, which I did not expect.
